subject: CCPA: edge-cache escrow plan and processor/agent boundary for interstate telemetry
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Heather Gomez <legal@heatherventures.com>
Cc: HeatherVentures Procurement <procurement@heatherventures.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed escrow pattern for edge caching + CCPA role

Hi Heather,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. Per our call, I wanted to put a concise proposal in writing so your legal and procurement teams can review:

- Redwood position: we operate as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA limited-use rules for customer content and telemetry tied to the contracted product.
- Edge caching: we use a CDN partner to cache short-lived inference payloads at the edge. That CDN will be listed as a subprocessor; cached content is TTL-limited and telemetry is pseudonymized where possible.
- Escrow option: for customers who need additional control, we can offer an escrow pattern where encryption keys for cached objects are escrowed with a customer-selected KMS or held in a neutral escrow (details below). This reduces live access by subprocessors.
- Onshore fallback: we can implement an onshore fallback for requests routed from US residents within a 30-day remediation window in the event of an incident or audit request.

I've attached a short outline (redwood-ccpa-escrow-outline.pdf) and a diagram stub we'll follow up with. If you want, we can draft a narrow DPA exhibit that captures the escrow flow and onshore fallback SLA.

Next steps proposed:
1) Confirm whether HeatherVentures prefers customer-managed KMS or a neutral escrow.
2) Procurement to confirm timeline constraints for implementation and whether key escrow adds procurement approvals.

Happy to hop on a quick call mid-week to walk the diagram.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-ccpa-escrow-outline.pdf (2 pages, summary)

From: Heather Gomez <legal@heatherventures.com>

Cc: HeatherVentures Procurement <procurement@heatherventures.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Proposed escrow pattern for edge caching + CCPA role

Sofia,

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifying questions from legal/procurement on first read:

1) Can you confirm the legal label you expect in the DPA (service provider vs processor)? Our California counsel will want explicit language that limits use to performing the services and prevents independent sale or cross-utility of data.
2) For the edge cache CDN: how long is TTL, what is cached (payload vs derived telemetry), and what controls exist to purge on request?
3) Escrow: what's the proposed escrow operator, and does escrow require us to pay an additional third-party fee?
4) Evidence: can you provide commensurate SOC2 report sections that show access controls to cached artifacts and key management attestations?

Procurement: please confirm our implementation window — we typically need DPA sign-off 6 weeks prior to go-live.

If it's helpful, our team can take a first pass on a narrow exhibit to attach to the DPA.

Thanks,
Heather Gomez
General Counsel
HeatherVentures

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Heather Gomez <legal@heatherventures.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:37:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Proposed escrow pattern for edge caching + CCPA role

Hi Heather / Sofia,

Quick technical clarifications from the infra side so your team has something concrete:
- TTL: default 60 seconds for raw inference blobs; 5 minutes for derived prompt-only summaries (configurable per customer).
- What we cache: we do not cache full PII-enriched profiles. Cached objects are request/response deltas and model KV prefixes where applicable (non-identifiers).
- Purge: we expose a canonical purge endpoint (API + console) and accept purge via webhook for large batches; applicable within the TTL window and with emergency purge within 2 hours for high-risk takedowns.
- Escrow operator: we support two patterns: (A) customer-managed KMS where keys never leave customer KMS and RR holds ciphertext; (B) neutral escrow (a third-party escrow custodian) where keys are held but require two-party release (customer + Redwood ops). Pattern A avoids third-party fees but requires KMS integration.
- Telemetry masking: before telemetry leaves our runtime we apply token-level hashing and redaction rules; for high-sensitivity customers we can attenuate sample rates and restrict retention.

I'll attach a quick dataflow diagram that maps cache nodes to jurisdiction boundaries.

— Jonas
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: telemetry-dataflow-diagram.png

Heather — appreciate the questions. Two commercial items to flag for procurement:
1) KMS integration (pattern A) is included in our enterprise plan if you provide access to the key material; neutral escrow (pattern B) will incur a one-time integration fee and a small monthly custody fee to the escrow provider. I can share ballpark numbers once procurement confirms a preference.
2) Onshore fallback (30-day window) is operationally feasible but may require a small reserved capacity add-on if HeatherVentures expects consistent high-throughput routing to onshore sites.

Sofia / Priya — can you confirm the exact DPA redline language we prefer for "service provider" labeling (we need to be careful with marketing/operational language vs legal binding terms).

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Proposed escrow pattern for edge caching + CCPA role

Team — summarizing the positions we should present back to HeatherVentures legal/procurement (so we have a single binding ask):

1) Legal label: Redwood accepts "Service Provider" (CCPA/CPRA limited-use) with explicit DPA language that disallows any "sale" or independent commercial reuse of customer personal data. We will add a short recital + limited-use section in the DPA exhibit.
2) Edge cache: CDN is a subprocessor. Default TTLs as Jonas described. We will include purge APIs and emergency purge SLA (2 hrs) in the exhibit.
3) Escrow patterns: Offer both patterns A (customer-managed KMS, no escrow fee) and B (neutral escrow with custody fee). For Pattern B, escrow release requires dual authorization.
4) Onshore fallback: commit to an operational onshore fallback within 30 days of a validated incident/audit trigger; include optional reserved-capacity pricing if HV expects ongoing routing.

Deliverables to customer: redlined DPA exhibit (attached), telemetry diagram, and a short SOC2 self-attestation excerpt relevant to access controls. Ask procurement for 6-week sign-off if they want to align to go-live.

I'll send the redline back to Heather with the exhibit language by EOD. Rafael — please confirm the fee ranges for escrow and reserved capacity so we can include them in procurement notes.

Priya Natarajan
Privacy & Data Protection Counsel
Redwood Inference
